A uniform bar of mass $M$ and length $L$ has three notches along the bottom. The center notch is at the center of mass of the bar, and the other two notches are a distance of $\frac{L}{12}$ on either side of the center notch. The bar is placed on a fulcrum as shown. A mass $M$, equal to the mass of the bar itself, is hung a distance $\frac{L}{4}$ from the right edge of the bar. When an unknown mass $M'$ is hung a distance $\frac{L}{4}$ from the left edge of the bar, the system remains in static equilibrium. Calculate the unknown mass 
\[M'\] in terms of 
\[M\].

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal uniform long strip, with three adjacent notches at the bottom. The top end of the triangular support contacts the leftmost notch among the three notches; the middle notch is marked as spaced L/12 relative to the notches on both sides, therefore the middle notch is the center-of-mass position of the rod, and the support is L/12 to the left of the center of mass. On the left side hangs an unknown mass M', whose hanging point is L/4 from the left end of the rod; on the right side hangs a mass M, whose hanging point is L/4 from the right end of the rod. Reasoning: Taking the center of the rod as x=0, then the left end of the rod is -L/2, and the right end is +L/2. The position of the left mass M' is -L/2+L/4=-L/4; the position of the right mass M is +L/2-L/4=+L/4; the rod's own weight M g acts at the center x=0. The support is at the left notch, with position x=-L/12. Relative to the support, the lever arm length of M' is |-L/4-(-L/12)|=L/6, located on the left side of the support; the lever arm of the rod's own weight is |0-(-L/12)|=L/12, located on the right side of the support; the lever arm of the right hanging mass M is |L/4-(-L/12)|=L/3, located on the right side of the support. Static equilibrium requires the counterclockwise torque to equal the clockwise torque: M'g(L/6)=Mg(L/12)+Mg(L/3). Eliminating g and L gives M'/6=M(1/12+1/3)=5M/12, so M'=6·5M/12=2.5M.

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: the triangular fulcrum contacts the left of the three bottom notches. The middle notch is the bar’s center of mass, and the right notch is another L/12 to the right, so the fulcrum is L/12 left of the bar’s center. From the text, the added mass M is hung L/4 from the right edge, so it is at x=+L/4 relative to the bar center; the unknown mass M' is hung L/4 from the left edge, so it is at x=-L/4. Take torques about the fulcrum at x=-L/12. The lever arms are: M' has distance L/6 to the left, the bar’s own weight M has distance L/12 to the right, and the right hanging mass M has distance L/3 to the right. Static equilibrium requires counterclockwise torque equals clockwise torque: M'g(L/6)=Mg(L/12)+Mg(L/3). Solve to get M'=2.5M.

The position of the left mass M' is -L/2+L/4=-L/4; the position of the right mass M is +L/2-L/4=+L/4; the rod's own weight M g acts at the center x=0. The support is at the left notch, with position x=-L/12. Relative to the support, the lever arm length of M' is |-L/4-(-L/12)|=L/6, located on the left side of the support; the lever arm of the rod's own weight is |0-(-L/12)|=L/12, located on the right side of the support; the lever arm of the right hanging mass M is |L/4-(-L/12)|=L/3, located on the right side of the support. Static equilibrium requires the counterclockwise torque to equal the clockwise torque: M'g(L/6)=Mg(L/12)+Mg(L/3). Eliminating g and L gives M'/6=M(1/12+1/3)=5M/12, so M'=6·5M/12=2.5M.
